_readme: One-line, sourced reasons for each city's latest AAI year-on-year change, shown in City Events > Air traffic. Only shown while 'month' matches the latest month in air-traffic.json; update it when a new month arrives. basis 'city' = a source names this city; 'national' = no city-specific cause published, so the national driver is shown and labelled as such. Cities left out have no verified cause.

all.text: The West Asia conflict disrupted Gulf flights, and high jet fuel prices led Air India (−22%) and IndiGo (−5–7%) to cut domestic flights from June to August.

national.text: Airlines cut domestic flights from June to August over high fuel costs (Air India −22%, IndiGo −5–7%); India's domestic traffic fell 6.3% in August.

delhi.text: Noida International Airport (Jewar) opened to commercial flights on 15 June 2026, adding new capacity to the NCR.

mumbai.text: Gulf flights from Mumbai were disrupted by the West Asia conflict, and Mumbai routes were among those cut from June to August over high fuel costs.

bengaluru.text: Delhi–Bengaluru was among the routes where Air India and IndiGo cut frequencies from June to August over high fuel costs.

hyderabad.text: Gulf traffic fell sharply amid the West Asia conflict (international −26%), and Delhi–Hyderabad frequencies were cut over fuel costs (domestic −13.6%).

kolkata.text: Delhi–Kolkata was among the routes where Air India and IndiGo cut frequencies from June to August over high fuel costs.

goa.text: Mopa airport traffic fell 22.8% in August, and Gulf flights were scaled back amid the West Asia conflict (Goa's international traffic down 42–69% in April–June).

jaipur.text: Airlines suspended seven domestic services from Jaipur in June 2026, citing low occupancy.

udaipur.text: Tourism and destination-wedding demand keep traffic rising (up 21% over the three years to FY2025-26).

ahmedabad.text: Mumbai–Ahmedabad was among the routes where Air India and IndiGo cut frequencies from June to August over high fuel costs.
